Hi Anya —

Thanks for the note and the context. Short answer: our default promo rules do not allow stacking two promotional credit pools that both reduce consumption billing (we enforce a single promotional credit application per account to avoid double-dipping). However, we frequently do programmatic exceptions for accelerator partners where there is an explicit carve-out and a defined controls/expiration window.

To make this operational (and to keep accounting/audit happy) we typically do one of the following:

- Option A — Stacking carve-out (temporary): we mark the cohort credit as a partner-sponsored overlay. Redwood applies the program credits first; LaunchLabs overlay pays (or backs) any overage credit usage. We require a short MOU and an explicit expiration date (we set it to the cohort end + 30 days).

- Option B — Promo conversion (preferred when procurement wants a clean bill): we convert LaunchLabs' USD 20k promo pool into a platform-side time-limited discount (e.g., 25% off usage for first 3 months up to $20k equivalent). This keeps us from applying two credit buckets in the billing system and is simpler for audits.

Operational asks from our side if you want an exception:
1) A partner-signed MOU (1 page) stating the overlay model and who bears the financial responsibility.
2) A list of participating accounts (emails) and their cohort start/end dates.
3) A one-time accounting contact to receive the final billing reconciliation (cc Priya).

I've attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a suggested pricing matrix that maps to both options. Ben and Priya are cc'd to comment on risk and accounting.

If you want, I can propose language for the MOU and the exact expiration fields.

Best,
